knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x - 1)}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8{(x - 1)}^{3} & =5 \\ {(x - 1)}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =5+8{(x - 1)}^{3} \\ \text{d}y & =(5{(x - 1)}^{-2}+8(x - 1))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \text{d}y & =\int (5{(x - 1)}^{-2}+8(x - 1))\,\text{d}x \\ y & =-5{(x - 1)}^{-1}+4{(x - 1)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(2)=6$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2) & =6 \\ -5(1)^{-1}+4(1)^{2}+C & =6 \\ C-1 & =6 \\ C & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =-5{(x - 1)}^{-1}+4{(x - 1)}^{2}+7 \\  & =-\frac{5}{(x - 1)}+4{(x - 1)}^{2}+7.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Separating the variables and integrating gives

$$y=\int\left(\frac{5}{(x-1)^2}+8(x-1)\right)\,\mathrm{d}x=-\frac{5}{x-1}+4(x-1)^2+C.$$

Apply $y(2)=7$: $-5+4+C=7$, so $C=8$. Thus

$$y=-\frac{5}{x-1}+4(x-1)^2+8.$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{3}$ that satisfies $y(3)=\frac{1}{8}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}(3{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{(x - 1)}^{3}) \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{(x - 1)}^{3} \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{(x - 1)}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =3\int {(x - 1)}^{2}\,\text{d}x-4\int {(x - 1)}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & ={(x - 1)}^{3}-{(x - 1)}^{4}+C \\ y & =\frac{1}{{(x - 1)}^{4}-{(x - 1)}^{3}-C}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(3)=\frac{1}{8}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(3) & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{{2}^{4}-{2}^{3}-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{8-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x - 1)}^{3}$ that satisfies the condition $y(3)=\frac{1}{8}$ is

$$
y=\frac{1}{{(x - 1)}^{4}-{(x - 1)}^{3}}\,.
$$
